findings.text: Advisory, as filed (Q10). Two doc comments sit stacked over memoryFeedUid, and the first only repeats the second. Both round-2 defects are fixed: underMirrorLease no longer hands `result` to `record` (mirror.ts:391-410), and purgeItem has no `actor` parameter or `"api"` branch (mirror.ts:635-656). I checked both against the code.
Advisory, as filed (Q5). runMirror and purgeItem are async but never await anything, so their callers in serve.ts await for nothing.
Advisory, as filed (Q2, boilerplate). The 404 `unknown` error is built here, again at push.ts:594, and inline at routes.ts:200.
Advisory, as filed (Q2, boilerplate). The alias lookup `deviceById(...)?.alias ?? ""` is written three times: here and at push.ts:486 and :620.
Advisory, as filed (Q3). eraseMemory returns revisions: 1, so the audit detail reads "memory: 1 revisions". The name does not match the value for that kind.

Advisory, as filed (Q1). The owed-replay test cannot tell whether the mark is written inside the erasure's transaction or only after the replay fails. The code writes it inside (mirror.ts:653), but the test does not pin that.
Advisory, carried over (Q5). The exact count of clock reads ties the test to the implementation, but the test still fails if the behaviour reverts.
Advisory, carried over. Reopening the file does not show that the earlier handle was closed.
Advisory, carried over. The no-wait timing is taken with an injected mirrorChild, before any child has launched.
Advisory, carried over as round 1 ruled. The file half of AC-54 sits under an observed criterion, so the item records no red run for it.

Advisory, as filed. setMeta overwrites the owed-replay note instead of merging it, so a second purge can drop a replay that an earlier purge still owes. I checked this in the code: purgeItem never reads owedReplay before it writes. The data gate upholds the same fact as a defect under its own rubric's personal-data question. Here it stays advisory as filed, because a judge does not raise a reviewer's severity.
Advisory, as filed. The TRUNCATE checkpoint can stall the server's writers for up to the 5 s busy timeout, twice per purge. The stall is bounded and only happens on the operator's command.
Advisory, as filed. On `wal: busy` the ADR says "the next checkpoint cuts it", but only a purge runs a truncating checkpoint, and the ADR names no operator step after `busy`.
Advisory, as filed. If an owed replay keeps failing, every run replays the folders again and holds the lease while it does. serve status shows this through mirror.last.
Advisory, carried over. A child that fails before it records anything, or a throw outside the per-revision blocks, leaves `error: null` or only a warn line. The next run heals it.
Advisory, carried over. publish depends on the docker job, which CI never runs. ADR Follow-ups names this.
Advisory, carried over. The version 0.7.0 is ahead of package.json, which is at 0.6.0.
Advisory, carried over (Q2). Rolling back across a schema bump is a manual restore, and the procedure is written down.
Advisory, carried over. The spec states that nothing consumes the HEALTHCHECK.

Advisory, as filed. "and nothing else of the module" is narrower than the code. The server also takes hashOf, projectFolderName, commitPaths, stagePaths, removePaths, slugify and entry.ts's format exports from the knowledge module. This is a wording issue, not a boundary crossed. The round-2 advisories are answered.
Advisory, as filed. The db.ts header and CLAUDE.md say "the two reads an open needs", while ADR 0026 now names four statements, the identity write among them.

Upheld (Q5, erasure of personal data not kept as the project states it). I checked this against the code. purgeItem writes REPLAY_MARK with setMeta, an upsert, from its own `touched` folders only. It never reads owedReplay first and never merges the note already there (mirror.ts:644-665). replayOwed then clears the mark once its own replay is whole (mirror.ts:553). Here is the sequence. Purge A commits its erasure, then its replay fails or is killed. Purge B runs before any mirror run. B overwrites A's note and clears it on success. The purged text of A stays in the git history of A's folders under repos/, and nothing records the debt any more. ADR 0026:78 says the next run finishes an owed replay, and that no longer holds. The line is new in this round, so it is inside the change. The fix: union the existing note with `touched` before writing it, or replay the owed folders first.

Advisory, as filed (Q2/Q6). With an index present, each batch of pendingRevisionsAfter reads and sorts every pending revision. That costs about P²/200 rows after --rebuild. The rubric calls a slower query with an index present an advisory.
Advisory, as filed (Q5). `checkpointWal(db) && cut` reports busy when either checkpoint truncated the log, and either one is enough. The report errs on the safe side but is wrong.
Advisory, as filed (Q5). "the next checkpoint cuts it" does not hold. The automatic checkpoint is PASSIVE, and nothing sets journal_size_limit.

Advisory, as filed (Q6). The TRUNCATE checkpoint holds off writers for up to the busy timeout, twice per purge. The stall is bounded and only happens on the operator's command, and the ADR does not mention it.
Advisory, as filed (Q4). The image is pushed before publish runs. ADR Follow-ups state the undo, and compose pins the version.
Advisory, as filed (Q1). The arm64 image never runs in the pipeline. ADR Follow-ups name this.
Advisory, as filed (Q6). The apt packages are not pinned by version. The base image is pinned by digest.
Advisory, debt outside the change. The profile's health command targets Caddy, not the server.
